TrackMachines.question: Duomatic machine is used for ___
TrackMachines.explanation: Duomatic is a continuous action tamping and lining machine (CATL) used for tamping (packing ballast under sleepers) and lateral alignment correction.

TrackMachines.question: BCM (Ballast Cleaning Machine) is used to ___
options: Clean and screen the existing dirty ballast
TrackMachines.explanation: BCM excavates the existing fouled ballast, screens/cleans it by removing fines and dirt, and returns cleaned ballast to the track.

TrackMachines.question: DTS (Dynamic Track Stabilizer) is used after tamping to ___
options: Increase train speed immediately after tamping
Consolidate ballast and achieve geometric stability quickly
TrackMachines.explanation: DTS applies controlled vibration and vertical load to the track after tamping to accelerate ballast consolidation and achieve early geometric stability.

TrackMachines.question: The speed restriction imposed after tamping by UNIMAT/Duomatic machine on BG is ___
TrackMachines.explanation: After tamping, a speed restriction of 30 kmph (engineering speed) is imposed until the track geometry consolidates sufficiently under traffic.

TrackMachines.question: FRM (Flashbutt Rail welding Machine) works on the principle of ___
TrackMachines.explanation: Flash butt welding works by passing heavy electric current through rail ends (resistance heating) until they reach welding temperature, then pressing them together.

TrackMachines.question: PQRS machine is used for ___
TrackMachines.explanation: PQRS (Profile Quality Rail Surface) machine is a rail grinding machine used to restore the correct rail head profile and remove corrugation.

TrackMachines.question: TRT (Tie Replacement Train) is used for ___
options: Replacing individual sleepers without disturbing track geometry much
TrackMachines.explanation: TRT is a mechanized sleeper replacement machine that removes old sleepers and inserts new ones continuously without removing ballast.

TrackMachines.question: Ballast Regulator (BR) is used to ___
options: Distribute and profile ballast along the track
TrackMachines.explanation: Ballast Regulator spreads, distributes and profiles ballast along the track, forming the correct cross-section after tamping or ballast delivery.

Establishment.question: The appointing authority for Group C railway employees is ___
Establishment.explanation: For Group C (erstwhile Group D promoted to C) railway employees, the appointing authority is the Senior Divisional Personnel Officer (Sr.DPO) at divisional level.

Establishment.question: Annual Confidential Report (ACR) of a Railway employee is written by ___
Establishment.explanation: ACR/APAR (Annual Performance Appraisal Report) is written by the immediate superior officer who is in the best position to assess daily performance.

Establishment.question: The maximum age limit for direct recruitment to Group C posts in Indian Railways is ___
Establishment.explanation: The upper age limit varies by post — typically 18-33 years for most Group C posts, with relaxations for SC/ST (5 years) and OBC (3 years).

Establishment.question: Earned Leave (EL) is credited at the rate of ___ days per year for railway employees.
Establishment.explanation: Earned Leave is credited at 30 days per year (2.5 days per month) to railway employees under the Leave Rules.

Establishment.question: Half Pay Leave (HPL) is credited at the rate of ___ days per year.
Establishment.explanation: Half Pay Leave is credited at 20 days per year (10 days per half year) to railway employees under the Leave Rules.

Establishment.question: The period for which Leave Not Due (LND) can be granted is limited to ___
Establishment.explanation: Leave Not Due can be granted for a maximum of 360 days during entire service, but not more than 180 days at one time.

Establishment.question: Commuted Leave can be taken as ___
options: Double the HPL on medical certificate
Establishment.explanation: Commuted Leave is granted as double the Half Pay Leave (HPL) balance on medical certificate, where HPL is debited half the commuted period.

Establishment.question: The minimum service required for eligibility for Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) in Indian Railways is ___
Establishment.explanation: An employee is eligible for VRS (Voluntary Retirement) after completing 20 years of qualifying service as per CCS Pension Rules.

Establishment.question: Leave Encashment on retirement: maximum number of EL days that can be encashed is ___
Establishment.explanation: A maximum of 300 days of Earned Leave can be encashed at the time of retirement (including superannuation, VRS, and death cases).

Establishment.question: A railway employee placed under suspension receives ___
Establishment.explanation: During suspension, an employee receives a subsistence allowance — typically 50% of basic pay for first 90 days, which may be revised thereafter.

Establishment.question: Which of the following is a Minor Penalty under Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules?
Establishment.explanation: Censure (written warning/reprimand) is a minor penalty. Major penalties include reduction in rank/pay, compulsory retirement, removal and dismissal.

Establishment.question: The appeal against an order imposing major penalty on a Group C employee lies with ___
Establishment.explanation: For Group C employees, appeal against major penalty orders lies with the General Manager of the Zonal Railway.

Establishment.question: Gratuity under Retirement Gratuity scheme is calculated as ___
options: One month's pay per year of service
Quarter month's pay per 6 months of qualifying service, max 16.5 times
Full month's pay for first 5 years
Establishment.explanation: Retirement Gratuity = (Basic Pay + DA) × 1/4 per 6 months of qualifying service, subject to maximum of 16.5 months' pay.

Establishment.question: DA (Dearness Allowance) is revised by Government ___
options: Twice a year (on 1 January and 1 July)
Establishment.explanation: DA is revised twice a year — effective from 1st January and 1st July — based on CPI (Industrial Workers) index to compensate for inflation.

Establishment.question: Casual Leave (CL) entitlement per year for a railway employee is ___
Establishment.explanation: Railway employees are entitled to 8 days of Casual Leave per calendar year (not encashable, not carried forward).

Finance_Stores.question: The purpose of a Budget is ___
options: An estimate of receipts and expenditures for the coming year, duly authorized
Finance_Stores.explanation: Budget is the annual financial statement presenting estimated receipts and expenditures for the coming financial year, approved by Parliament/authority.

Finance_Stores.question: As per Indian Railways financial rules, the financial year is from ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: The Indian Government/Railways financial year runs from 1st April to 31st March of the next calendar year.

Finance_Stores.question: Imprest Cash is maintained for ___
options: Small and urgent petty cash expenditures
Finance_Stores.explanation: Imprest Cash (Petty Cash) is a small fixed amount given to officials to meet urgent, small day-to-day expenses without going through regular bill procedure.

Finance_Stores.question: The competent authority for sanction of works costing up to ₹10 crore in Indian Railways is ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) has financial powers to sanction works up to certain limits; for ₹10 crore level works, it typically falls within DRM/PHOD powers.

Finance_Stores.question: Tenders are invited for procurement of stores worth more than ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: As per DGS&D/Railway procurement norms, open/limited tenders are invited for purchases above ₹2 lakhs; below this, purchases may be made through limited quotations.

Finance_Stores.question: Stock verification in railways is done by ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: Physical stock verification in railway stores depots is conducted by Finance Inspectors (from accounts/finance wing) to ensure accuracy of stock records.

Finance_Stores.question: The document authorizing release of material from railway stores is called ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: An Issue Note (also called Issue Voucher or Material Issue Note) is the document that authorizes release of materials from the stores to the requisitioning authority.

Finance_Stores.question: BG (Budget Grant) in railway finance refers to ___
options: Budgetary Grant approved by Parliament for specific heads of expenditure
Finance_Stores.explanation: Budgetary Grant (BG) is the amount approved by Parliament under various heads of account that authorizes expenditure up to that limit.

Finance_Stores.question: Advance Correction Slip (ACS) is issued to ___
options: Update and amend railway codes and manuals
Finance_Stores.explanation: ACS (Advance Correction Slip) is issued to make advance amendments to railway codes, manuals and schedules before they are formally revised.

Finance_Stores.question: Dead Stock in railway stores refers to ___
options: Items that are non-consumable (furniture, equipment, machinery)
Finance_Stores.explanation: Dead Stock refers to non-consumable, durable items like furniture, equipment, machinery, and tools that are used repeatedly and not consumed in one use.

Finance_Stores.question: The EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) for tenders in Indian Railways is generally ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) is typically 2% of the estimated cost of the contract, submitted with the tender to ensure seriousness of the bidder.

Finance_Stores.question: Security Deposit from contractors in Indian Railways is ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: Security Deposit (SD) from contractors is deducted at 10% of the gross bill amount (or 5% upfront + 5% deducted) to ensure performance of the contract.

Finance_Stores.question: Scrap materials in railway stores are disposed by ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: Scrap and unserviceable materials are disposed of through public auction or open tender to get the best market price.

Finance_Stores.question: The ceiling on cash purchase by a JE/AEN without tender formalities is ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: As per delegation of financial powers, a JE/AEN level officer can make spot/cash purchases up to ₹10,000 without tender formalities for urgent requirements.

Finance_Stores.question: Pensionary benefits in Indian Railways are regulated by ___
Finance_Stores.explanation: Pension for railway employees is governed by Railway Services (Pension) Rules 1993, which is specific to railway servants.

GeneralKnowledge.question: The total route length of Indian Railways (approx.) is ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: Indian Railways has a total route length of approximately 68,000 km, making it one of the largest rail networks in the world.

GeneralKnowledge.question: Indian Railways was nationalised in ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: All the various private and state railway companies were nationalised and merged into a single entity — Indian Railways — in 1951-1953.

GeneralKnowledge.question: The highest railway station in India is ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: Ghum (also spelt Ghoom) station on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway at 2,258 m above sea level is the highest railway station in India.

GeneralKnowledge.question: DFC (Dedicated Freight Corridor) in India is being implemented by ___
options: DFCCIL (Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd.)
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: DFCCIL (Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited) is the special purpose vehicle set up by the Government of India to implement the DFC project.

GeneralKnowledge.question: RITES stands for ___
options: Rail India Technical and Economic Service
Railway Infrastructure and Technical Engineering Service
Rail India Transport and Economic Systems
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: RITES (Rail India Technical and Economic Service) is a PSU under the Ministry of Railways providing transport infrastructure consulting and project management.

GeneralKnowledge.question: The first railway in India ran between ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: The first passenger train in India ran between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane on 16th April 1853, covering 34 km.

GeneralKnowledge.question: The zonal headquarters of South Central Railway is ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: South Central Railway (SCR) has its zonal headquarters at Secunderabad (Hyderabad).

GeneralKnowledge.question: The Railway Protection Force (RPF) is under the administrative control of ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: RPF (Railway Protection Force) is a security force established under the Railways Act and is under the administrative control of the Ministry of Railways.

GeneralKnowledge.question: Konkan Railway connects ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: Konkan Railway connects Roha (Maharashtra) to Mangaluru (Karnataka) along the western coast, covering approximately 741 km.

GeneralKnowledge.question: The first metro rail in India was commissioned in ___
GeneralKnowledge.explanation: Kolkata Metro was the first metro rail system in India, inaugurated in 1984 between Dumdum and Belgachia stations.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: The target fixed in Annual Programme for giving answer in Hindi for the letters received in Hindi is ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: As per Official Language Policy, replies to letters received in Hindi must be sent in Hindi — the target is 100%.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Which Ministry issues important policy decisions pertaining to Official Language?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: The Department of Official Language under the Ministry of Home Affairs issues policy decisions, circulars and instructions on Official Language matters.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Official Languages Rules were framed in year ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: The Official Languages Rules were framed in 1976 under the Official Languages Act 1963 to give effect to the Act's provisions.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: As per the Constitution of India, the form of numerals to be used for official purposes of the Union shall be ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Article 343 of the Constitution specifies that International form of Indian numerals (1,2,3...) shall be used for official purposes of the Union.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Who works as the Chairman of Central Hindi Committee?
options: Chairman of the Parliamentary committee on Rajbhasha
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: The Central Hindi Committee (Kendriya Hindi Samiti) is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: The award given for writing original books in Hindi on technical Railway subjects is ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri Technical Puraskar is awarded by Indian Railways to employees who write original technical books in Hindi on railway subjects.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Which of the following is NOT an incentive given to Railway employees for passing Hindi examinations?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Out-of-turn promotion is NOT given for passing Hindi exams. Cash awards, lump sum awards, and personal pay are the incentives provided.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: When did section 3(3) of the Official Language Act take effect?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Section 3(3) of the Official Language Act 1963 (mandating bilingual issue of documents like orders, notices, etc.) took effect from 26 January 1965.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: How many sub-committees are there in the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language has 4 sub-committees to examine different aspects of Hindi implementation.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Who is the Chairman of the Official Language Implementation Committee of the Divisional Railway Office?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: The Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) is the Chairman of the Official Language Implementation Committee at the Divisional level.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: When was Sindhi language added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Sindhi language was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution by the 21st Constitutional Amendment in 1967.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: The foreign language that is included in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India is ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Nepali language is listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. While Nepali is spoken across borders, it is recognized as a language of Indian communities in Sikkim and northeastern India.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: Who was the first Chairman of the committee formed on the recommendation of the Official Language Commission?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Govind Ballabh Pant was the first chairman of the committee formed on the recommendation of the Official Language Commission.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: The name of the award given for writing Hindi poetry books is ___
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: Prem Chand Puraskar is awarded for writing original Hindi poetry/literature books, named after the famous Hindi writer Munshi Premchand.

Hindi_Rajbhasha.question: How many languages were included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution when it was adopted?
Hindi_Rajbhasha.explanation: At the time the Indian Constitution was adopted in 1950, 14 languages were listed in the Eighth Schedule. Currently there are 22 scheduled languages.

Surveying.question: The principle of surveying is ___
options: To work from part to whole
To work from whole to part
To work from any convenient starting point
Surveying.explanation: The fundamental principle of surveying is to work from whole to part — establish overall control first, then fill in details. This minimizes accumulation of errors.

Surveying.question: The instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles in surveying is ___
Surveying.explanation: A Theodolite measures both horizontal angles (for bearing) and vertical angles (for elevation/depression), making it the primary angular measurement instrument.

Surveying.question: Fly levelling is done ___
options: For precise levelling of important structures
To carry levels quickly over long distances between two points
Surveying.explanation: Fly levelling rapidly carries levels from one benchmark to another over long distances. Accuracy is less than precise levelling but speed is high.

Surveying.question: GPS in surveying stands for ___
Surveying.explanation: GPS (Global Positioning System) uses satellite signals to determine precise three-dimensional coordinates of any point on earth's surface.

Surveying.question: The formula for length of a circular curve is ___
Surveying.explanation: Length of circular curve L = (πRΔ)/180, where R = radius in meters and Δ = deflection angle in degrees. This converts arc angle to arc length.

Surveying.question: Ranging in chain surveying is done to ___
options: Establish intermediate points on a survey line between two endpoints
Surveying.explanation: Ranging establishes a series of intermediate ranging rods in a straight line between two survey stations, allowing accurate measurement along the survey line.

Surveying.question: The instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles in surveying:
Surveying.explanation: Theodolite measures horizontal angles, vertical angles, deflection angles, magnetic bearings — primary angular measurement instrument.

Surveying.question: In levelling, the Height of Instrument (HI) is calculated as:
Surveying.explanation: Height of Instrument HI = RL of benchmark + Back Sight reading (BS).

Surveying.question: The arithmetic check in levelling is:
options: ΣBS − ΣFS = Last RL − First RL
Surveying.explanation: Arithmetic check: ΣBS − ΣFS = Last RL − First RL (also ΣBS − ΣFS = ΣRise − ΣFall).

Surveying.question: In chain surveying, the 'Base Line' is defined as:
options: Longest line running through middle of area
Surveying.explanation: Base Line: the longest and most prominent chain line running through the middle of the survey area.

SOM.question: The stress-strain curve for a mild steel specimen shows ___
options: A well-defined yield point and upper/lower yield points
SOM.explanation: Mild steel shows a characteristic stress-strain curve with a well-defined upper and lower yield point, followed by plastic deformation and strain hardening.

SOM.question: Young's Modulus of Elasticity (E) for structural steel is approximately ___
SOM.explanation: Young's Modulus of elasticity for structural steel is approximately 200-210 GPa (2×10⁵ MPa), used in structural calculations.

SOM.question: A simply supported beam with UDL (uniformly distributed load) of w per unit length and span L has maximum bending moment at ___
SOM.explanation: For a simply supported beam with UDL, maximum BM occurs at mid-span = wL²/8. At supports the BM is zero.

SOM.question: Factor of Safety (FOS) is defined as ___
SOM.explanation: FOS = Ultimate stress / Permissible stress. It represents the ratio of the material's maximum capacity to the actual working stress.

SOM.question: Which of the following is a statically indeterminate structure?
SOM.explanation: A continuous beam over 3 or more supports is statically indeterminate as the number of unknowns exceeds the available equilibrium equations.

SOM.question: How do short columns primarily fail?
SOM.explanation: Short columns fail due to direct compressive (crushing) stress when the material's ultimate compressive strength is exceeded, without significant buckling.

SOM.question: A structural member subjected to axial compressive force in any orientation is called:
SOM.explanation: A strut is a compression member in any orientation; a column is specifically vertical.

SOM.question: The rate of change of Shear Force along a beam section equals:
SOM.explanation: As per basic beam theory dV/dx = w (load intensity). The rate of change of SF equals the load intensity at that section.

SOM.question: The rate of change of Bending Moment along a beam equals:
SOM.explanation: The fundamental differential equation dM/dx = V states rate of change of BM equals shear force.

SOM.question: Shape of Shear Force Diagram for a beam under UDL:
SOM.explanation: For UDL the shear force varies linearly, resulting in an inclined straight line SFD.

SOM.question: Shape of Shear Force Diagram for a beam under UVL (Uniformly Varying Load):
SOM.explanation: For UVL load intensity varies linearly, causing the SFD to be parabolic.

SOM.question: Bending Moment diagram shape for a cantilever beam with a point load at free end:
SOM.explanation: BM increases linearly from zero at free end to maximum at fixed support — triangular shape.

SOM.question: Effect of a concentrated couple (moment) on the Shear Force Diagram:
SOM.explanation: A concentrated couple causes no change in SFD; it only produces a sudden jump in the BMD.

SOM.question: The point where bending moment changes sign along a beam is called:
SOM.explanation: Point of Contraflexure is where BM is zero and changes sign.

SOM.question: Graph showing variation of a force effect at a point as a unit load moves across the span:
SOM.explanation: An Influence Line Diagram shows how a response (reaction, moment, shear) at a specific point varies as a unit load traverses the span.

SOM.question: Material property allowing large plastic deformation before fracture, enabling wire drawing:
SOM.explanation: Ductility is the ability to deform plastically before fracture, essential for wire drawing.

SOM.question: The safe design stress legally allowed, kept below elastic limit:
SOM.explanation: Working stress is the permissible stress that a material can safely carry during service.

SOM.question: Mechanical test to determine a metal's resistance to sudden impact shocks:
SOM.explanation: Impact tests (Izod, Charpy) measure toughness — the energy absorbed during high-rate loading.

SOM.question: Mechanical test to determine a material's capacity to resist cyclic stress variations without cracking:
SOM.explanation: Fatigue tests evaluate behaviour under repeated/fluctuating stresses — critical for rotating components.

SOM.question: Moment of Inertia for a rectangular section (b × d) about its centroidal axis (Ixx):
SOM.explanation: The area moment of inertia of a rectangle about its centroidal axis parallel to base = bd³/12.

SOM.question: Moment of Inertia for a solid circular section of diameter d:
SOM.explanation: Area moment of inertia of a solid circle about its centroidal axis = πd⁴/64.

SOM.question: Shape of Bending Moment diagram for a simply supported beam carrying UDL:
SOM.explanation: For SS beam with UDL, BM varies parabolically with maximum at centre and zero at supports.

SOM.question: Shape of Shear Force diagram for a simply supported beam with point load at mid-span:
SOM.explanation: SF is constant on each side of the point load with a sudden drop, creating rectangular shapes on each side.

SOM.question: For a cantilever beam with UDL, the Bending Moment diagram is:
SOM.explanation: BM varies as the square of the distance from the free end — parabolic.

SOM.question: At the point of contraflexure, the bending moment is:
SOM.explanation: Point of contraflexure is where BM changes sign — its value is zero at that point.

SOM.question: Which of the following is a statically determinate beam?
SOM.explanation: A simply supported beam has 3 unknowns and 3 equilibrium equations → statically determinate.

SOM.question: The unit of moment of inertia (area moment) is:
SOM.explanation: Moment of inertia = area × distance² → m² × m² = m⁴.

SOM.question: Section modulus (Z) for a rectangular section of width b and depth d:
SOM.explanation: Z = I/y_max = (bd³/12)/(d/2) = bd²/6.

SOM.question: Which of the following is a measure of a material's stiffness?
SOM.explanation: Young's Modulus (E) relates stress to strain in the elastic range, defining resistance to deformation.

SOM.question: Hooke's law holds up to which point on the stress-strain curve?
SOM.explanation: Hooke's law (stress ∝ strain) is valid only up to the proportional limit.

SOM.question: The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is called:
SOM.explanation: Poisson's ratio ν = −(lateral strain)/(longitudinal strain).

SOM.question: A material that fails in tension with very little plastic deformation is called:
SOM.explanation: Brittle materials (cast iron, glass, concrete) fracture suddenly with negligible plastic strain.

SOM.question: The theoretical maximum value of Poisson's ratio for an isotropic material is:
SOM.explanation: For an incompressible material (e.g., rubber), Poisson's ratio approaches 0.5.

SOM.question: The modulus of rigidity (G) is defined as the ratio of:
SOM.explanation: Shear modulus G = τ/γ (shear stress / shear strain).

SOM.question: The relationship between E, G and K (elastic constants):
SOM.explanation: Both E = 2G(1+μ) and E = 3K(1-2μ) are standard elastic constants relationships.

SOM.question: The maximum deflection in a simply supported beam with central point load occurs at:
SOM.explanation: Due to symmetry, maximum deflection under a central point load is at mid-span.

SOM.question: The slope of the elastic curve at a point in a beam equals:
SOM.explanation: Slope θ = ∫(M/EI)dx from the moment-curvature relationship of beams.

RCC_Steel.question: The minimum grade of concrete recommended for RCC structures as per IS 456 is ___
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456:2000 recommends M20 (20 MPa characteristic compressive strength) as the minimum grade for general RCC structures.

RCC_Steel.question: Water-cement ratio has a direct effect on ___
RCC_Steel.explanation: W/C ratio is the most important factor affecting both workability (higher W/C → more workable) and strength (lower W/C → higher strength) of concrete.

RCC_Steel.question: Cover to reinforcement in concrete is provided to protect against ___
RCC_Steel.explanation: Adequate concrete cover protects steel reinforcement from corrosion (moisture and carbonation) and also provides fire resistance.

RCC_Steel.question: The slump test for concrete measures ___
RCC_Steel.explanation: The slump test measures the workability/consistency of fresh concrete — how easily it flows and fills the formwork.

RCC_Steel.question: In a doubly reinforced beam, compression reinforcement is provided to ___
options: Reduce depth when depth is restricted and single reinforcement is insufficient
RCC_Steel.explanation: Doubly reinforced beams are used when beam depth is restricted and the moment exceeds the capacity of a singly reinforced section.

RCC_Steel.question: As per IS 456, the maximum water-cement ratio for moderate exposure conditions is ___
RCC_Steel.explanation: For moderate exposure conditions (as per IS 456:2000 Table 5), the maximum W/C ratio is 0.50.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum clear cover for an RCC slab (IS 456)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 specifies minimum clear cover of 15 mm for slabs, not less than bar diameter.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum clear cover for an RCC beam (IS 456)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 prescribes nominal cover of 25 mm for beams, subject to durability.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum clear cover for an RCC column (IS 456)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 specifies nominal cover of 40 mm for columns.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum clear cover for a foundation footing (IS 456)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 specifies minimum 50 mm clear cover for footings to protect against soil contact.

RCC_Steel.question: Maximum final setting time for OPC as per IS 269?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 269 prescribes a maximum final setting time of 600 minutes (10 hours) for OPC.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum initial setting time for OPC as per IS 269?
RCC_Steel.explanation: OPC must have initial setting time of at least 30 minutes to allow mixing, transporting, and placing.

RCC_Steel.question: Grade range for 'Standard Concrete' as per IS 456:2000?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456:2000 Table 2 classifies M25 to M55 as Standard Concrete.

RCC_Steel.question: What does M20 concrete specification mean?
options: Minimum characteristic strength of 20 N/mm² at 28 days
RCC_Steel.explanation: M20 → characteristic compressive strength (fck) = 20 N/mm² at 28 days; not more than 5% of cubes fail below this.

RCC_Steel.question: Standard slump range for mass concrete works?
RCC_Steel.explanation: For mass concrete (foundations), slump of 25-75 mm provides adequate workability for placement.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum stripping time for side formwork of columns and beams?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Vertical formwork is removed after 16-24 hours once concrete gains enough strength to hold its own weight.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum stripping time for props supporting slabs up to 4.5 m span?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 specifies minimum 7 days for props under slabs with span < 4.5 m.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum stripping time for props supporting beams with spans up to 6.0 m?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 specifies minimum 14 days for props under beams with span < 6 m.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum curing period for concrete when blended cements are used?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Blended cements (PPC, PSC) gain strength slowly; IS 456 recommends 14 days curing.

RCC_Steel.question: Number of concrete cube samples required for a batch volume of 31-50 m³?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 Table 1: for 31-50 m³ concrete quantity, 4 samples are required.

RCC_Steel.question: Field NDT test to measure surface hardness of concrete?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Rebound Hammer (Schmidt Hammer) measures surface hardness correlating to compressive strength.

RCC_Steel.question: Field NDT test to measure internal homogeneity of concrete?
RCC_Steel.explanation: UPV test sends ultrasonic pulses through concrete to detect voids, cracks, and inhomogeneities.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum bar diameter for main longitudinal reinforcement in an RCC column?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 mandates minimum 12 mm diameter for column longitudinal bars to prevent buckling.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum number of longitudinal bars in a circular RCC column?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456: for circular or helical reinforced columns, minimum 6 longitudinal bars required.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum thickness for an RCC slab as per standard codes?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Standard codes specify minimum 125 mm slab thickness for adequate stiffness and fire resistance.

RCC_Steel.question: Standard design density for Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Unit weight of RCC is taken as 25 kN/m³ (2500 kg/m³) accounting for steel reinforcement.

RCC_Steel.question: Maximum permissible diameter of rebar in an RCC slab of thickness 't'?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Bar diameter in a slab is limited to t/8 to prevent excessive cracking and ensure proper cover.

RCC_Steel.question: Maximum reinforcement area percentage permitted in an RCC beam (IS 456)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 cl.26.5.1 restricts total steel in a beam to 4% of gross cross-sectional area.

RCC_Steel.question: What side face reinforcement is needed if RCC beam depth exceeds 750 mm?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 cl.26.5.1.3: for webs deeper than 750 mm, side face reinforcement controls web cracking.

RCC_Steel.question: At what height is a counterfort retaining wall typically used?
RCC_Steel.explanation: For walls > 6 m, bending moments become large; counterforts connect stem to base slab for economy.

RCC_Steel.question: Standard single commercial length of a reinforcing steel rod?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Standard length of commercial TMT/HYSD bar is 12 metres for handling and transport.

RCC_Steel.question: Beyond what diameter is manual lap splicing not recommended on Indian Railways?
RCC_Steel.explanation: For bars > 36 mm diameter, mechanical couplers or welding are required for proper load transfer on Indian Railways.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum 28-day cube strength for pre-tensioned concrete (IS 1343)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 1343:2012 specifies minimum M45 (45 N/mm²) for pre-tensioned concrete.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum 28-day cube strength for post-tensioned concrete (IS 1343)?
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 1343:2012 specifies minimum M35 (35 N/mm²) for post-tensioned concrete.

RCC_Steel.question: What does Abrams' water-cement ratio law state?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Abrams' Law: strength of concrete is primarily a function of its water-cement ratio for workable mixes.

RCC_Steel.question: Definition of Characteristic Strength (fck)?
options: Strength below which not more than 5% of test results fall
RCC_Steel.explanation: fck: value of compressive strength below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall.

RCC_Steel.question: Three standard laboratory tests for workability of concrete?
options: Sieve analysis, Slump test, Vee-Bee test
Slump test, Vee-Bee test, Compaction factor test
Compression test, Slump test, Compaction factor test
Tensile test, Vee-Bee test, Slump test
RCC_Steel.explanation: Slump test, Vee-Bee consistometer test, and Compaction factor test are the three standard workability tests.

RCC_Steel.question: If L/B ratio of a slab > 2, it is designed as:
RCC_Steel.explanation: Slabs with aspect ratio L/B > 2 are one-way slabs; they primarily bend in the short direction.

RCC_Steel.question: If L/B ratio of a slab ≤ 2, it is designed as:
RCC_Steel.explanation: Slabs with L/B ≤ 2 are two-way slabs — loads transfer in both directions to supports.

RCC_Steel.question: An RCC beam where actual neutral axis depth exceeds critical neutral axis depth:
RCC_Steel.explanation: Over-reinforced beam: concrete crushes before steel yields — sudden brittle failure (undesirable).

RCC_Steel.question: Three classical Post-Tensioning systems?
RCC_Steel.explanation: Classical post-tensioning systems: Freyssinet system, Magnel-Blaton system, Lee-McCall system.

RCC_Steel.question: A beam is said to be 'under-reinforced' when:
options: Steel does not yield at all
RCC_Steel.explanation: Under-reinforced beams fail by steel yielding first — ductile failure with prior warning.

RCC_Steel.question: In a doubly reinforced beam, the additional steel is provided in the:
RCC_Steel.explanation: Compression reinforcement is added in compression zone to increase moment capacity when section size is limited.

RCC_Steel.question: The neutral axis depth in a balanced RC beam is determined by:
options: Steel yield strain and concrete ultimate strain
RCC_Steel.explanation: Balanced condition: steel reaches yield strain exactly when concrete reaches ultimate strain (0.0035 per IS 456).

RCC_Steel.question: The term 'effective depth' of a beam means:
options: Distance from compression face to centroid of tension reinforcement
Distance between tension and compression reinforcement
Depth up to centre of beam
RCC_Steel.explanation: Effective depth d = overall depth – clear cover – half bar diameter.

RCC_Steel.question: Depth of equivalent rectangular stress block for RCC beam as per IS 456:
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456:2000: depth of rectangular stress block = 0.42 × neutral axis depth (xu).

RCC_Steel.question: Limiting neutral axis depth (xu,max) for Fe415 steel (IS 456):
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 cl.38.1: for Fe415 steel, xu,max/d = 0.48.

RCC_Steel.question: A beam is called 'deep beam' when its span-to-depth ratio is less than:
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456: beams with clear span < 2 × effective depth are designed as deep beams.

RCC_Steel.question: Purpose of providing stirrups in a beam:
options: Resist shear stress and diagonal tension
RCC_Steel.explanation: Stirrups (vertical or inclined links) resist shear and diagonal tensile cracks in beams.

RCC_Steel.question: Development length of a bar depends on:
options: Bar diameter, steel stress, and bond strength
RCC_Steel.explanation: Ld = (φ σs)/(4 τbd) — depends on bar diameter φ, steel stress σs, and design bond stress τbd.

RCC_Steel.question: A short column is one for which slenderness ratio (leff/least lateral dimension) is less than:
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456: column is short if leff/D < 12; otherwise it is slender and buckling must be considered.

RCC_Steel.question: Helical reinforcement in a column increases its load capacity by approximately:
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 allows 5% increase in load-carrying capacity for columns with helical confinement reinforcement.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum eccentricity to be considered in design of axially loaded columns (IS 456):
options: Greater of (l/500) and (D/30) but not less than 20 mm
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 cl.25.4: minimum eccentricity = max(l/500, D/30) with a minimum of 20 mm.

RCC_Steel.question: Critical section for maximum BM in a cantilever retaining wall:
options: Junction of stem with base slab
RCC_Steel.explanation: Maximum bending moment in retaining wall stem occurs at its junction with the base slab.

RCC_Steel.question: Minimum factor of safety against sliding for a retaining wall:
RCC_Steel.explanation: IS 456 and IR practice: FOS against sliding ≥ 1.5 for retaining walls.

SoilMechanics.question: The shear strength of cohesionless soil (sand) depends on ___
SoilMechanics.explanation: In cohesionless soils like sand, cohesion c = 0, so shear strength depends entirely on the angle of internal friction (φ) and normal stress.

SoilMechanics.question: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) is used to determine ___
SoilMechanics.explanation: SPT gives N-value which is used to estimate bearing capacity of soil, soil classification, and degree of compaction in the field.

SoilMechanics.question: Terzaghi's theory of consolidation is related to ___
options: Time-dependent settlement of saturated clay under load
SoilMechanics.explanation: Terzaghi's consolidation theory describes the time-dependent process of pore water pressure dissipation and corresponding settlement in saturated clays under sustained load.

SoilMechanics.question: The angle of repose of a soil is ___
options: Equal to angle of internal friction
The slope angle at which a soil heap remains stable without support
The angle of maximum shear stress
SoilMechanics.explanation: Angle of repose is the steepest angle at which a granular material will remain stable on its own without any support — approximately equal to angle of internal friction for dry sand.

SoilMechanics.question: Atterberg limits are used to classify ___
SoilMechanics.explanation: Atterberg limits (Liquid Limit, Plastic Limit, Shrinkage Limit) are applicable to fine-grained soils (silts and clays) to define their consistency and plasticity.

SoilMechanics.question: Soil with minimum coefficient of permeability:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Clay has very small pore spaces and high surface friction — extremely low permeability compared to granular soils.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Plastic Limit (Wp):
options: Water content at which soil flows
Water content at which soil crumbles when rolled into 3 mm thread
Water content at which soil volume changes
Water content at which soil is saturated
SoilMechanics.explanation: Plastic Limit: water content below which soil stops behaving plastically and begins to crumble.

SoilMechanics.question: Classification of Under-Reamed Piles:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Under-reamed piles are bored, cast-in-situ concrete piles with enlarged bulb(s) at bottom for uplift resistance.

SoilMechanics.question: Height of application of active earth pressure resultant on a retaining wall:
SoilMechanics.explanation: For level backfill, resultant active earth pressure acts at H/3 above base of retaining wall.

SoilMechanics.question: Field test to determine safe bearing capacity and settlement:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Plate Load Test: load applied to steel plate at foundation level; settlement measured to estimate bearing capacity.

SoilMechanics.question: Moisture boundary between plastic and liquid state of soil:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Liquid Limit (LL): water content at which soil behaviour transitions from plastic solid to liquid mass.

SoilMechanics.question: Formula for Plasticity Index (Ip):
SoilMechanics.explanation: Plasticity Index Ip = LL − PL (range of moisture over which soil remains plastic).

SoilMechanics.question: Contact pressure distribution under a rigid footing on clay:
options: Maximum at centre, minimum at edges
Minimum at centre, maximum at edges
SoilMechanics.explanation: Rigid footing settles uniformly; for clay, contact pressure is higher at edges to maintain uniform settlement.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
options: Gross pressure at which soil fails in shear
Safe pressure a soil can carry
Net pressure a soil can carry
Pressure at which footing settles 25 mm
SoilMechanics.explanation: Ultimate Bearing Capacity (q_ult): minimum gross pressure at foundation base causing shear failure in soil.

SoilMechanics.question: Deep foundation adopted underwater for heavy bridge piers:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Caisson/well foundations are large watertight structures sunk into place — ideal for deep underwater bridge piers.

SoilMechanics.question: For which soil type are under-reamed piles best suited?
SoilMechanics.explanation: Under-reamed piles designed for expansive soils like Black Cotton Soil; resist swelling/shrinkage movements.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Porosity (n) in soil:
options: Ratio of voids to solids volume
Ratio of water to voids volume
Ratio of voids to total volume
Ratio of solids to total volume
SoilMechanics.explanation: Porosity n = Vv/V (volume of voids / total volume of soil).

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Voids Ratio (e) in soil:
options: Ratio of voids to total volume
Ratio of voids to solids volume
Ratio of water to voids volume
Ratio of water to solids volume
SoilMechanics.explanation: Void ratio e = Vv/Vs (volume of voids / volume of solids).

SoilMechanics.question: Formula for Uniformity Coefficient (Cu):
SoilMechanics.explanation: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 — measures range of particle sizes in soil.

SoilMechanics.question: Formula for Coefficient of Curvature (Cc):
SoilMechanics.explanation: Cc = (D30)²/(D10 × D60) — describes shape of particle size distribution curve.

SoilMechanics.question: Range of Coefficient of Curvature (Cc) for a well-graded soil:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Well-graded soil has Cc between 1 and 3, indicating smooth gradation of particle sizes.

SoilMechanics.question: Compaction equipment for cohesive clay soils:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Sheep foot roller's kneading action is ideal for compacting cohesive soils like clay.

SoilMechanics.question: Particle size range of Silt as per IS classification:
SoilMechanics.explanation: IS classification: silt particles range from 0.002 mm to 0.075 mm.

SoilMechanics.question: Maximum loose layer thickness for embankment construction on Indian Railways:
SoilMechanics.explanation: IR specification: earthwork in embankments laid in horizontal layers not exceeding 300 mm (30 cm) loose.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Optimum Moisture Content (OMC):
options: Water content for maximum dry density
SoilMechanics.explanation: OMC: specific moisture content at which soil is compacted to maximum dry density for a given compactive effort.

SoilMechanics.question: Temporary watertight enclosure built underwater for construction:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Coffer dam: temporary structure excluding water to create dry working area for foundation construction.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Shrinkage Limit in soil:
options: Water content at which volume decreases
Water content at which cracks appear
Water content below which no further volume change occurs
Water content at which soil becomes liquid
SoilMechanics.explanation: Shrinkage Limit: water content at which further loss of moisture produces no decrease in soil volume.

SoilMechanics.question: Definition of Permeability of soil:
options: Ability to permit water to pass through voids
SoilMechanics.explanation: Permeability: property of porous material allowing fluids to flow through interconnected voids.

SoilMechanics.question: Standard spacing between bulbs in an under-reamed pile:
SoilMechanics.explanation: IS 2911: clear spacing of 1.5 times shaft diameter between successive bulbs for effective load transfer.

SoilMechanics.question: Shallow foundation with network of steel I-beams on weak soils:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Grillage foundation: tiers of steel I-beams in grid pattern embedded in concrete to distribute heavy loads.

SoilMechanics.question: Laboratory method for grain size distribution of fine-grained soil (< 75 µm):
SoilMechanics.explanation: For particles finer than 75 µm, sedimentation-based Hydrometer or Pipette analysis is used.

SoilMechanics.question: Uniformity Coefficient (Cu) for well-graded gravel:
SoilMechanics.explanation: IS 2720: for well-graded gravel, uniformity coefficient Cu > 4.

SoilMechanics.question: Uniformity Coefficient (Cu) for well-graded sand:
SoilMechanics.explanation: IS 2720: for well-graded sand, uniformity coefficient Cu > 6.

SoilMechanics.question: Foundation designed as a continuous thick slab to counter differential settlement:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Raft/mat foundation: large concrete slab over entire footprint, minimises differential settlement.

SoilMechanics.question: Laboratory apparatus to determine OMC and Maximum Dry Density:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Standard Proctor Compaction Test (IS 2720 Part 7) determines OMC and Maximum Dry Density.

SoilMechanics.question: Coefficient of active earth pressure (Ka) for level backfill with φ = 30°:
Coefficient of passive earth pressure (Kp) for φ = 30°:
Vertical cut in cohesive soil (φ = 0) can stand unsupported up to height of:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Critical height Hc = 4c/γ for φ = 0 soil (c = cohesion, γ = unit weight).

SoilMechanics.question: The liquid limit of a soil is determined using:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Casagrande's liquid limit apparatus (grooving tool and cup) is the standard method.

SoilMechanics.question: A soil has a plasticity index of zero. It is most likely:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Non-plastic soils (Ip = 0) include sands and gravels — no plastic behaviour.

SoilMechanics.question: The standard Proctor test gives maximum dry density at which water content?
SoilMechanics.explanation: OMC corresponds to the peak dry density on the Proctor compaction curve.

SoilMechanics.question: In a consolidation test, Cv is determined using:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Both Taylor's square root of time method and Casagrande's log t method are used to find Cv.

SoilMechanics.question: The ultimate settlement of a foundation on clay is due to:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Total settlement = immediate (elastic) compression + primary consolidation + secondary (creep) consolidation.

SoilMechanics.question: Bearing capacity of soil improves if the water table:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Lowering water table increases effective stress in soil → increases bearing capacity.

SoilMechanics.question: A pile is called a 'friction pile' if it transfers load primarily by:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Friction piles rely on shaft resistance (skin friction) along their length to carry loads.

SoilMechanics.question: Negative skin friction on a pile occurs when:
options: Surrounding soil settles more than the pile
SoilMechanics.explanation: Downdrag (negative skin friction) occurs when soft compressible soil settles, pulling the pile down.

SoilMechanics.question: The group efficiency of piles in sand is generally:
SoilMechanics.explanation: In sand, pile group efficiency > 1 due to densification effect of adjacent piles.

SoilMechanics.question: Standard Penetration Number (N) is blows required to drive sampler for:
options: Next 300 mm after 150 mm seating drive
SoilMechanics.explanation: N = number of blows for 300 mm penetration after initial 150 mm seating drive.

SoilMechanics.question: For normally consolidated clay, coefficient of earth pressure at rest (K0):
SoilMechanics.explanation: Jaky's formula: K0 = 1 − sinφ for normally consolidated soils.

SoilMechanics.question: Critical hydraulic gradient (ic) for quick sand condition:
SoilMechanics.explanation: ic = (G−1)/(1+e), where G = specific gravity of soil solids, e = void ratio.

SoilMechanics.question: In a triaxial test, the cell pressure represents the:
SoilMechanics.explanation: In triaxial test: σ3 = cell pressure (confining stress); σ1 = σ3 + deviator stress.

SoilMechanics.question: Vane shear test is most suitable for measuring undrained shear strength of:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Vane shear test is used for soft to medium cohesive soils, especially sensitive clays.

SoilMechanics.question: The angle of repose of a soil is approximately equal to its:
SoilMechanics.explanation: Angle of repose ≈ φ for dry cohesionless soil — slope angle at which granular material is stable.

SoilMechanics.question: In a flow net, the region between two successive flow lines is called a:
SoilMechanics.explanation: A flow channel is the area bounded by two adjacent flow lines in a flow net.

SoilMechanics.question: Phreatic line in an earth dam is the:
options: Line of zero pore pressure only
Both top-most flow line and line of zero pore pressure
SoilMechanics.explanation: The phreatic line is the top flow line where pore pressure = atmospheric (zero gauge pressure).

SoilMechanics.question: Factor of safety against boiling (quick sand) is defined as:
SoilMechanics.explanation: FOS against quicksand = critical hydraulic gradient (ic) / actual hydraulic gradient (i).

PHE.question: As per IRWM, the amount of residual chlorine in public water supply for safety against pathogenic bacteria is about ___
PHE.explanation: Residual chlorine of 0.2 mg/L at the consumer end is maintained to ensure water remains safe against pathogenic bacteria during distribution.

PHE.question: Provision of septic tanks with soak pit/filter bed is NOT appropriate for toilets of colony in ___
PHE.explanation: In heavily built-up urban areas, septic tanks are unsuitable due to space constraints and the availability of municipal sewage systems.

PHE.question: For design of sewage system, as per IRWM, ___ of water supplied is considered to reach sewers.
PHE.explanation: IRWM specifies that 75% of the daily water supply should be taken as the sewage flow rate for sewer design purposes.

PHE.question: The most effective method of disinfection of water supply is ___
PHE.explanation: Chlorination is the most common and cost-effective method of disinfection of water supply, providing residual protection during distribution.

PHE.question: BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is an indicator of ___
options: Degree of organic pollution in water
PHE.explanation: BOD measures the amount of dissolved oxygen consumed by microorganisms when decomposing organic matter — a higher BOD indicates more pollution.

PHE.question: Daily water supply requirement per head for residential quarters on Indian Railways?
PHE.explanation: IRWM specifies 200 litres per capita per day (lpcd) for residential areas.

PHE.question: Design water allocation for non-residential passengers at railway stations?
PHE.explanation: For non-residential passengers, design allocation is 25 litres per person per day.

PHE.question: Where are air valves positioned in a water pipeline?
PHE.explanation: Air valves at high points (summits) automatically release trapped air that reduces flow efficiency.

PHE.question: Where are scour valves (blow-off valves) installed in a water pipeline?
PHE.explanation: Scour valves at low points and dead ends allow removal of sediment and draining for maintenance.

PHE.question: Minimum Residual Chlorine required at the farthest point of water supply network?
PHE.explanation: IS 10500: free residual chlorine of at least 0.2 mg/l must be maintained throughout distribution system.

PHE.question: Colorimetric field test to check residual chlorine:
PHE.explanation: OT test: orthotolidine reacts with chlorine to produce yellow-brown colour indicating chlorine concentration.

PHE.question: Acceptable pH range for drinking water (IS 10500/BIS):
PHE.explanation: BIS/IS 10500 specifies desirable pH range of 6.5 to 8.5 for drinking water.

PHE.question: Percentage of water supplied that reaches sewer as sewage:
PHE.explanation: Standard assumption: 80% of water supplied returns as sewage (losses from consumption, evaporation, leakage).

PHE.question: Minimum self-cleaning velocity in sanitary sewers:
PHE.explanation: Self-cleansing velocity of at least 0.6 m/s prevents settlement and deposition of solids in sewers.

PHE.question: Maximum permissible velocity in sewers to prevent scouring:
PHE.explanation: Maximum design velocity in sewers limited to 2.0 m/s to prevent scouring of pipe material.

PHE.question: Minimum inside diameter for a public sewer in plain areas:
PHE.explanation: Minimum diameter for public sewer is 200 mm to prevent clogging and allow maintenance.

PHE.question: Filtration rate for Slow Sand Filters:
PHE.explanation: Slow sand filters operate at low rate of 100–200 litres/hour/m² of filter area.

PHE.question: Filtration rate for Rapid Sand Filters:
PHE.explanation: Rapid sand filters operate at 3000–6000 litres/hour/m², much higher than slow sand filters.

PHE.question: Available chlorine content in commercial bleaching powder:
PHE.explanation: Bleaching powder used for water disinfection contains approximately 30–35% available chlorine.

PHE.question: Time for heating a public tap mouth before collecting a water sample for bacteriological analysis:
PHE.explanation: Tap mouth must be flamed for ~5 minutes to sterilise it and eliminate surface contaminants before sampling.

PHE.question: Chamber on a sewer line for inspection and cleaning:
PHE.explanation: A manhole provides access for inspection, maintenance, cleaning, and testing of sewer system.

PHE.question: Trap provided to collect sullage from bathrooms and kitchens:
PHE.explanation: Floor trap (Nahni trap) collects wastewater from floors while water seal prevents foul gases entering.

PHE.question: Desired pH for effective disinfection by chlorination:
PHE.explanation: Chlorine most effective at pH < 7 as HOCl (hypochlorous acid) dominates — stronger disinfectant than OCl⁻.

PHE.question: Maximum permissible cleaning interval for a septic tank:
PHE.explanation: Septic tanks should be cleaned at least once a year to remove accumulated sludge and scum.

PHE.question: Field test to verify the safe yield of an open well:
PHE.explanation: Recuperation test: pump well down, measure rate of water level recovery to calculate safe yield.

PHE.question: Suspended impurities in water cause which physical characteristic?
PHE.explanation: Turbidity caused by suspended particles (silt, clay, organic matter) that scatter light — cloudy appearance.

PHE.question: Category of impurities that act as source of water-borne diseases:
PHE.explanation: Pathogenic bacteria and viruses (colloidal size) are responsible for water-borne diseases like cholera, typhoid.

PHE.question: Type of hardness caused by sulfates and chlorides of Ca and Mg:
PHE.explanation: Permanent hardness (non-carbonate) caused by chlorides and sulfates of Ca/Mg — cannot be removed by boiling.

PHE.question: Type of hardness caused by carbonates and bicarbonates of Ca and Mg:
PHE.explanation: Temporary hardness (carbonate hardness) from dissolved bicarbonates — can be removed by boiling.

PHE.question: Water softening processes for removing permanent hardness:
PHE.explanation: Lime-Soda process uses chemical precipitation; Zeolite/Base-Exchange uses ion-exchange to remove Ca/Mg.

PHE.question: Standard conditions for BOD test:
PHE.explanation: Standard BOD₅ test: 5 days at 20°C in the dark (incubation period and temperature standardised globally).

PHE.question: Rapid methods for testing a sewer for leaks and blockages before commissioning:
options: Air test, Water test, Smoke test
PHE.explanation: Before commissioning: air test (integrity), water test (leaks), smoke test (detect defects/illegal connections).

PHE.question: Comparison of COD and BOD for the same wastewater sample:
PHE.explanation: COD measures oxygen to oxidize all organic matter (biodegradable + non-biodegradable); COD ≥ BOD always.

PHE.question: Standard slope provided for bathroom floors towards the outlet:
PHE.explanation: Bathroom floors sloped at 1 in 60 towards floor trap — ensures drainage without uncomfortably steep slope.

PHE.question: Standard slope for passenger platform surfaces on Indian Railways:
PHE.explanation: Railway platforms sloped at 1 in 60 so rainwater drains quickly without pooling.

PHE.question: Purpose of providing water-sealed traps in sanitary pipe layout:
options: Allow air to enter the pipe
Prevent entry of foul sewer gases into buildings
PHE.explanation: Water seal trap retains water in pipe bend creating barrier preventing foul gases and insects entering buildings.

PHE.question: Maximum allowable turbidity for drinking water (IRWM/IS 10500)?
PHE.explanation: IRWM and IS 10500 specify turbidity should not exceed 10 NTU for drinking water.

PHE.question: Minimum depth of water seal required in a sanitary trap:
PHE.explanation: Minimum 50 mm water seal depth is standard for sanitary traps — effective barrier against foul gases.

PHE.question: Pump type selected for tube wells with a small discharge diameter:
PHE.explanation: Submersible pumps placed directly inside the well are most efficient for small-diameter tube wells.

PHE.question: Class of bacteria that decomposes sludge in an anaerobic septic tank:
PHE.explanation: Septic tank is anaerobic (no oxygen); anaerobic bacteria decompose sludge into gases, liquids, and stable matter.

ConstructionMat.question: Initial setting time of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) should NOT be less than ___
ConstructionMat.explanation: As per IS 269, the initial setting time of OPC should not be less than 30 minutes. This allows sufficient time for mixing, transporting and placing.

ConstructionMat.question: The specific gravity of OPC (Ordinary Portland Cement) is approximately ___
ConstructionMat.explanation: The specific gravity of Ordinary Portland Cement is approximately 3.15, used in mix design calculations.

ConstructionMat.question: Seasoning of timber is done to ___
options: Reduce moisture content to prevent warping, cracking and decay
ConstructionMat.explanation: Seasoning removes excess moisture from timber to prevent warping, shrinkage, cracking, and decay during service.

ConstructionMat.question: The IS code for classification of Indian timber is ___
ConstructionMat.explanation: IS 399 classifies commercial Indian timbers and provides their physical and mechanical properties for structural use.

Hydraulics.question: Froude number is the ratio of ___
Hydraulics.explanation: Froude number (Fr) = V/√(gL) represents the ratio of inertial forces to gravitational forces. Fr<1 is subcritical, Fr>1 is supercritical flow.

Hydraulics.question: The formula for discharge over a rectangular sharp-crested weir (without end contractions) is ___
Hydraulics.explanation: Francis' formula: Q = 1.84 L H^(3/2) (SI units) for discharge over a rectangular sharp-crested weir where L = length, H = head of water.

Hydraulics.question: Manning's formula for flow velocity in open channels is ___
Hydraulics.explanation: Manning's formula: V = (1/n) × R^(2/3) × S^(1/2), where n = Manning's roughness coefficient, R = hydraulic radius, S = slope.

Hydraulics.question: The return period of a design flood for a major bridge on Indian Railways is generally taken as ___
Hydraulics.explanation: Design floods for major railway bridges are typically based on a 100-year return period flood to ensure adequate safety.

Hydraulics.question: Froude Number for critical flow in an open channel:
Hydraulics.explanation: Critical flow (minimum specific energy for given discharge) is characterised by Froude number = 1.

Hydraulics.question: Definition of Hydraulic Radius in an open channel:
Hydraulics.explanation: Hydraulic radius R = Cross-sectional area / Wetted perimeter, key parameter in Manning's equation.

Hydraulics.question: Definition of Hydraulic Depth in an open channel:
Hydraulics.explanation: Hydraulic depth D = Cross-sectional flow area / Top width of water surface.

Hydraulics.question: Froude Number for super-critical flow:
Hydraulics.explanation: Supercritical flow is high-velocity shallow flow where Froude number > 1.

Hydraulics.question: Froude Number for sub-critical flow:
Hydraulics.explanation: Subcritical flow is tranquil, low-velocity flow where Froude number < 1.

Hydraulics.question: A sudden rise in water level when flow changes from super-critical to sub-critical:
Hydraulics.explanation: Hydraulic jump: high-velocity supercritical flow abruptly changes to low-velocity subcritical flow, dissipating energy.

Hydraulics.question: Condition for the most economical rectangular channel:
Hydraulics.explanation: For hydraulically efficient rectangular channel (minimum wetted perimeter), bottom width b = 2 × depth d.

Hydraulics.question: Graph showing river discharge vs. time is called:
Hydraulics.explanation: A hydrograph plots discharge of a river over time, typically in response to a rainfall event.

Hydraulics.question: X-axis coordinate in a standard hydrograph:
Hydraulics.explanation: In a hydrograph, time (hours or days) is plotted on X-axis and corresponding discharge on Y-axis.

Hydraulics.question: Empirical formula for flood discharge in North and Central India:
Hydraulics.explanation: Dicken's Formula Q = C × A^(3/4) is used for estimating flood discharge in North and Central India.

Hydraulics.question: Empirical formula for flood discharge in South India:
Hydraulics.explanation: Ryves Formula Q = C × A^(2/3) is adopted for flood estimation in southern India.

Hydraulics.question: Which drainage basin shape produces a larger peak runoff?
Hydraulics.explanation: Fan-shaped basin: runoff from all parts converges at outlet simultaneously — higher peak discharge.

Hydraulics.question: Fluid property that offers resistance to shear stress:
Hydraulics.explanation: Viscosity is the measure of a fluid's resistance to shear stress — its internal friction.

Hydraulics.question: Effect of temperature increase on dynamic viscosity of liquids:
Hydraulics.explanation: For liquids, increased temperature lowers intermolecular cohesive forces → viscosity decreases.

Hydraulics.question: Effect of temperature increase on dynamic viscosity of gases:
Hydraulics.explanation: In gases, viscosity arises from molecular momentum transfer; more collisions at higher temperature → viscosity increases.

Hydraulics.question: Definition of an Ideal Fluid:
Hydraulics.explanation: An ideal fluid is theoretical: zero viscosity (inviscid) and incompressible.

Hydraulics.question: Condition for laminar flow in a pipe (Reynolds Number):
Hydraulics.explanation: Flow is laminar when Re < 2000; viscous forces dominate and layers flow in parallel.

Hydraulics.question: Condition for steady flow:
options: Quantity flowing per second is constant over time
Hydraulics.explanation: Steady flow: mass/volumetric flow rate past any point is constant with respect to time.

Hydraulics.question: Definition of a Prismatic Channel:
options: Constant bed slope and constant cross-section
Hydraulics.explanation: A prismatic channel has constant shape, size, and bed slope along its length.

Hydraulics.question: Formula for Specific Energy (E) in an open channel:
Hydraulics.explanation: Specific energy E = y + V²/2g (depth + velocity head, relative to channel bottom).

Hydraulics.question: Definition of Critical Depth in open channels:
options: Depth at which velocity is maximum
Depth at which specific energy is minimum for a given discharge
Depth at which Froude number is zero
Depth at which discharge is minimum
Hydraulics.explanation: Critical depth yc: depth of flow at which specific energy is minimum for a given discharge.

Hydraulics.question: The rise in water level upstream of a bridge is called:
Hydraulics.explanation: Afflux: increase in water level upstream caused by constriction of river at bridge opening.

Hydraulics.question: Maximum permissible design afflux on Indian Railways?
Hydraulics.explanation: Indian Railways Bridge Manual restricts permissible afflux to 150 mm for bridge structures.

Hydraulics.question: Instrument used to measure stream flow velocity:
Hydraulics.explanation: A current meter measures velocity of flow in open channels and streams.

Hydraulics.question: Flood frequency for major bridge design on Indian Railways:
Hydraulics.explanation: Per IRBM Para 2.2, major bridges are designed for 50-year return period flood.

Hydraulics.question: Percentage increase in design flood discharge for small catchments (< 500 sq. km):
Hydraulics.explanation: A 30% increase is applied to calculated design discharge for small catchments as a safety margin.

Hydraulics.question: Low walls at bridge entry and exit to reduce scouring are:
Hydraulics.explanation: Drop walls break the fall of water at inlet; curtain walls at outlet extend deep to prevent scour.

Hydraulics.question: Law for determining water flow velocity through an aquifer:
Hydraulics.explanation: Darcy's Law: flow rate through porous medium is proportional to hydraulic gradient and permeability.

Hydraulics.question: According to Lacey's regime theory, the silt factor is directly proportional to:
options: Square root of average particle size
Hydraulics.explanation: Lacey's silt factor f ∝ √d (square root of average particle size d).

Hydraulics.question: 'Piping' in hydraulic structures refers to:
options: Boiling of sand due to upward seepage
Hydraulics.explanation: Piping: upward seepage forces reduce effective stress, causing sand to boil and flow — progressive erosion.

Miscellaneous.question: The speed restriction imposed on a railway track after deep screening of ballast is ___
Miscellaneous.explanation: After deep screening, a 30 kmph speed restriction is imposed until adequate consolidation under traffic is achieved and track geometry stabilizes.

Miscellaneous.question: G&SR stands for ___
Miscellaneous.explanation: G&SR (General and Subsidiary Rules) are rules framed under the Railway Act governing the working of trains, signals, and safety on Indian Railways.

Miscellaneous.question: Block working in railways refers to ___
options: A method of working where only one train occupies a block section at a time
The maintenance block for track works
Miscellaneous.explanation: Block system ensures only one train at a time is allowed in a block section (between two block stations), providing basic safety against collision.

Miscellaneous.question: The authority for a train to enter a block section is ___
options: Line Clear token/authority given by Station Master
Miscellaneous.explanation: A train can enter a block section only after obtaining a Line Clear token/authority from the station master, ensuring the section is clear.

Miscellaneous.question: Works requiring temporary single line working (TSL) need a sanction from ___
Miscellaneous.explanation: Temporary Single Line working affecting train operations requires sanction of the Divisional Engineer (DE/AEN in coordination with DEN).

Miscellaneous.question: As per G&SR, the maximum speed over a temporary speed restriction (TSR) imposed by engineering department is ___
options: As specified in the TSR notice
Miscellaneous.explanation: The speed of TSR is specified in the Engineering Speed Restriction notice issued by the SE/SSE and published in the Special Train Notice.

Miscellaneous.question: An Engineering Caution Order is given to the driver ___
options: When speed restriction is imposed over 15 kmph
When speed restriction is 15 kmph or below
Miscellaneous.explanation: A written Caution Order (CA) is given to the driver at the station preceding the restriction point when the restricted speed is 15 kmph or below.

Miscellaneous.question: A 'Fit to run certificate' for OHE (Overhead Equipment) maintenance is given by ___
Miscellaneous.explanation: Fit-to-run (resumption of traffic) after OHE maintenance work is certified by TRD (Traction-Electrical) Department officer.

Miscellaneous.question: The correct sequence of shunting movements at a station is ___
options: Check line clear → Set points → Signal → Move
Miscellaneous.explanation: Safe shunting sequence: verify line is clear, set/check points correctly, obtain signal authority, then move the vehicles.

Miscellaneous.question: Trolley refuge is provided near tracks to ___
options: Provide shelter for track men in case of approaching trains
Miscellaneous.explanation: Trolley refuges are small shelters built adjacent to the track at regular intervals where track-men and trolleys can take shelter when trains approach.

Miscellaneous.question: The detonators in railways are used as ___
options: Warning signals to alert drivers of danger ahead
Miscellaneous.explanation: Detonators (fog signals) are placed on rails to give an audible warning to loco pilots by exploding under wheel pressure, alerting them to danger ahead.

Miscellaneous.question: As per IRPWM, the gang patrolman (track watchman) should patrol his beat ___
options: Only during fog and heavy rain
Miscellaneous.explanation: Gang patrolmen continuously patrol their assigned beats, with increased vigilance during monsoon, fog, and after heavy rains to detect track damage.

Miscellaneous.question: Which document records the details of all trains running on a railway section?
Miscellaneous.explanation: A train graph (or train working graph) is a graphical representation of all trains scheduled on a section, showing their movements against time.
